nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What challenges do food industry actors face when aligning with the Farm-to-Fork strategy for sustainable food production?
nodes.answer: The industry may encounter difficulties in adjusting production methods, sourcing sustainable ingredients, and meeting changing consumer demands for eco-friendly products.

nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What is the primary focus of the paragraph regarding true cost accounting in relation to agriculture?
nodes.answer: The primary focus is on understanding true cost accounting and the true cost of food production, acknowledging the unaccounted externalities of food, fibre, and fuel production in the context of health and sustainability.
nodes.paragraph: This compliments the understanding of true cost accounting and the true cost of food framing found elsewhere in health and sustainability discourse (Hendriks et al. 2023; Richardson 2021). These more comprehensive framings of agricultural sustainability acknowledge the unaccounted-for externalities of food, fibre, and fuel production (Pretty et al. 2001). Acknowledging that intersections and overlaps between pillars exist (Purvis et al. 2019), this comprehensive framing is supported by argu- ments for measuring other agricultural system elements, including up-stream and down-stream factors. Using the food system as an example, these arguments include nutri- tion and food safety considerations of food production aside the environmental considerations ( akmak et al. 2023), and the inadequacy in current social indicators in sustainable food production metrics (Orou Sannou et al. 2023). Further, the role of responsible governance has been highlighted as important for transition to sustainable food (Kozar et al. 2023 ), fibre, and fuel systems (Bentsen et al. 2019 ) with gov - ernance disclosures in sustainability reporting mechanisms shown to impact positively on the market performance of agricultural products (Buallay 2022).

nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Which country is the leading producer of lentils and peas in the world?
nodes.answer: Canada is the leading producer of lentils and peas.

The inclu- sion of pulses into simplified rotations is a widely adopted diversification strategy (Hufnagel et al. 2020), as legumes can provide an array of ecological benefits (Ditzler et al. 2021). Some examples are improved N use efficiency (St. Luce et al. 2015), N credit from biological fixation (Bell et al. 2017; Taveira et al. 2020), increased water conserva- tion (Gan et al. 2017; Seymour et al. 2012), reduced N2O emissions (Lemke et al. 2007; Liu et al. 2024), improved soil health (Lal 2017), and enhanced biodiversity (Zander et al. 2016). These valuable ecosystem services encourage farmers to include pulse crops into cereal and oilseed rotations, par - ticularly in semi-arid cropping systems, where limited water availability presents significant challenges to sustainability. Canada leads global lentil and pea production, yielding 2.9 million tonnes of lentils and 4.6 million tonnes of peas in 2021, which accounts for 45% and 31% of world produc - tion (FAO 2024).

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does sustainable agriculture ensure long-term profitability?
nodes.answer: Sustainable agriculture ensures long-term profitability by optimizing resource use and minimizing reliance on nonrenewable inputs.
nodes.paragraph: Sustainable agriculture Sustainable agriculture represents a holistic approach to farming, aiming to meet current food needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs(Altieri et al. 2017 ; Gomiero et al. 2011 ; Kout - souris 2009 ; Lichtfouse et al. 2009 ; Mason 2003 ; Muhie 2022 ; Rajput et al. 2023 , 2024 ; Velten et al. 2015 ). It inte - grates three primary goals: environmental health, eco - nomic profitability, and social equity(Chen et al. 2021 ; Czy ewski and Kryszak 2022 ; D nmez et al. 2024 ; Velten et al. 2015 ). Practices such as crop rotation, agroforestry, and organic farming play a pivotal role in maintain - ing soil health, reducing erosion, and enhancing biodiversity(Lekberg et al. 2024 ; Ngaba et al. 2024 ; Tully and McAskill 2020 ). By optimizing resource use and minimizing reliance on nonrenewable inputs, sustainable agriculture ensures long-term profitability(D nmez et al. 2024 ). nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the features of sustainable food production in terms of reducing environmental impacts?
nodes.answer: Sustainable food production aims to reduce environmental impacts through the effective utilization of material, energy, and manufacturing processes.

nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How is the economic aspect correlated with sustainable food production?
nodes.answer: The economic aspect of sustainable food production involves risk assessment and reduction, the birth of enterprises, and the development of low-cost and high-profit food products.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does sustainable food production differ from traditional food production?
nodes.answer: Sustainable food production embraces emerging technologies and practices to achieve continuous improvement, unlike traditional food production methods. This innovation and adaptation characteristic aim to meet current generation needs without compromising future generations' capacity to fulfil their own needs.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does environmental stewardship in sustainable food production aim to minimize environmental impact?
nodes.answer: Environmental stewardship in sustainable food production aims to minimize environmental impact through strategies like greenhouse gas emissions reduction, soil erosion minimization, and water conservation.

nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How does sustainable development in agriculture, according to Plus, balance the use of natural resources with food production?
nodes.answer: Plus suggests that sustainable development in agriculture involves programming farming production to reasonably use natural resources while providing sufficient food of high quality.
